title: Chromosome mutations and polyploidy; Natural selection
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EV01a#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE07#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV01a#N.6b, GE07#N.6b, EV01a#N.11, GE07#N.10, EV01a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mutation
items.clue: The original source of all new alleles; it arises at random

items.label: Evolution
items.clue: A change in the allele frequencies of a population over time

items.label: Fitness
items.clue: Reproductive success: leaving surviving offspring that go on to breed

items.label: Non-disjunction
items.clue: Failure of a pair to separate in meiosis, so both go to the same pole.

questions.stem: Researchers followed four individuals in a population of a hypothetical bird species throughout their lives. Which individual had the greatest evolutionary fitness?

options.text: A small female that lived 3 years and produced 9 offspring that survived to breed
A large male that won every fight he entered and fathered 2 offspring that survived to breed
A female that lived 9 years, the longest of all, and produced 4 offspring that survived to breed
A female that lived 4 years and produced 30 offspring, none of which survived to breed

questions.explanation: Fitness is measured by reproductive success. Her 9 breeding offspring are more than any other individual's, despite her small size and short life.

questions.stem: In an adult of a hypothetical mammal, nondisjunction occurs in two cells: during mitosis in a skin cell, and during meiosis in a cell in the testes that gives rise to sperm. Which prediction about the effects of these two errors is best supported?

options.text: Both errors can be passed to the adult's children, as each changes the adult's chromosomes
The error in mitosis gives every cell of the adult's body an abnormal chromosome number
Neither error can affect a child, as fertilization restores the normal chromosome number
Only the error in meiosis can give a child an abnormal chromosome number in every cell

questions.stem: A population of 50 plants contains 8 RR, 24 Rr and 18 rr. What is the frequency of allele R?
questions.explanation: 50 plants carry 100 alleles. R = 2 × 8 + 24 = 40, so its frequency is 40 ÷ 100 = 0.40.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical animal, a segment carrying several genes breaks off one copy of chromosome 4 and is lost, while the rest of that chromosome remains in the cell. Which statement best explains why this change can lead to a genetic disorder?

options.text: The cell has lost a whole copy of chromosome 4, so every gene on that chromosome is now missing
Each gene in the segment now has a point mutation, which can change the protein it codes for
Each gene in the lost segment is left with one copy, which can alter the amount of its product
Every gene after the break point on chromosome 4 is now read in a shifted reading frame

questions.stem: A student builds a flowchart model of how natural selection increased the mean beak depth of a population of a hypothetical seed-eating bird species over several generations of drought. Which flowchart best represents this process?

options.text: Birds vary in heritable beak depth → seeds are scarce → deep-beaked birds leave more offspring → mean beak depth rises
Birds crack hard seeds → their beaks deepen with use → their offspring inherit the deeper beaks → mean beak depth rises
Birds vary in beak depth → seeds are scarce → each bird's beak deepens over its life → mean beak depth rises
Drought begins → the drought causes new deep-beaked variants to arise → these birds then survive → mean beak depth rises
